story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: How were the crowds then? It was a quite popular --
Oh, it was a quite popular place.
I know a lot of people from out of town would come there.
That's right.
Big names, and things. Sort of like a small scale Grand Terrace in that respect, wasn't it?
Yes, it was. Only real small, real small place.
He had started out with, I think, Miff Mole was in the band, and Sidney Bechet.
Yeah, Sidney Bechet.
And wasn't Sid --
Sid Catlett worked with him. Oh, a number of famous jazz musicians worked with Jazz Limited.
And then he went to like an all-Chicago band, regular band, and stopped using --
Started using Chicago musicians, right.
Was the repertoire pretty much the same then as it'd always been with Bill?
Same thing.
How would the tempo --
Same tempos.
But with Freddie Koblmann, it might have been a little --
Well, Freddie knew more about what he wanted, you know, being from New Orleans.
Were there any out of the ordinary things that happened in that band when you were with them in the early sixties?
No, I can't think of anything. Regular-regulation jazz music, and good musicians.
